h: Turning a park day into a Suffolk break
p: Pleasurewood Hills is a full-day sort of place. Between the rides, the animal presentations and the shows, most families find they need from opening until mid-afternoon at least, so it's worth arriving early and getting a couple of the most popular rides done before the queues build.

Pack a picnic if you want to keep costs down, and bring a small bag you can stash easily, because you won't want to be juggling coats and carrier bags on every ride. Layers are your friend on the Suffolk coast: a sunny morning can turn breezy by the afternoon.

With a mix of ages, try splitting the group for a while. One grown-up takes the thrill-seekers to the big rides, the other stays with the younger ones on the family attractions, then meet up for a show. Everyone gets their fix and nobody spends the day standing at an exit gate holding the bags.

If you're staying in the area, there's lots more to see. Ness Point in Lowestoft marks the most easterly spot in the UK and makes a fun photo stop. Oulton Broad, on the edge of town, is the southern gateway to the Norfolk and Suffolk Broads, perfect for a boat trip or a waterside stroll. Africa Alive! at Kessingland, just south of Lowestoft, is a great follow-up day for animal lovers, and Great Yarmouth's busy seafront is a short drive up the coast.
Lowestoft's South Beach is sandy and a lovely place to wind down after a day of rides.
